packs.name: Whitespace
packs.description: Characters that take up space, or claim to, and are impossible to see in a form.

values.name: Trailing space
values.breaks: Login and e-mail comparisons differ between browser and server; the account is created but cannot be found.
values.expect: Trimmed everywhere or preserved everywhere - never one on sign-up and the other on sign-in.

values.name: Leading space
values.breaks: Sorting puts the record at the top of every list, and exact-match search never finds it.
values.expect: Same trimming rule as everywhere else in the application.

values.name: A single space
values.breaks: The browser counts the field as filled and the server counts it as empty, or the other way round.
values.expect: One consistent verdict on both sides about whether this field is empty.

values.name: Three zero-width spaces
values.breaks: Character counters, comparison and deduplication see a different value than the human does.
values.expect: Stored and returned unchanged, or rejected with a message that names the characters.

values.name: Non-breaking space between words
values.breaks: Search for a plain-space spelling never finds the record; exports and mail merges keep the invisible difference forever.
values.expect: Treated as a space by search, or normalised on save - consistently.

values.name: Newline in a single-line field
values.breaks: A single-line field that accepts a line break breaks CSV export, log lines and every list view below it.
values.expect: Rejected, or stored with the break preserved and escaped on export.

values.name: Tab inside a value
values.breaks: Tab-separated exports split one record into two columns; column alignment in reports collapses.
values.expect: Rejected or escaped on export - never passed through raw into a delimited format.

values.name: Carriage return and newline inside a value
values.breaks: Two line-ending conventions in one field make the same text compare as different across systems.
values.expect: Normalised to one convention on save, or preserved and escaped consistently.

values.name: A single zero-width space
values.breaks: A field that looks empty but is not: required-field validation passes, and the record has no usable name.
values.expect: Treated as empty by validation, or shown in a way that reveals the field is not empty.

values.name: Ogham space mark
values.breaks: A character in the space category that renders as a visible line - it breaks both trimming and layout assumptions.
values.expect: Handled like any other whitespace character, or rejected with a message.

values.name: Three spaces between words
values.breaks: Search, deduplication and printed output treat runs of spaces inconsistently between layers.
values.expect: Collapsed on save or preserved on save - one rule, applied everywhere.

values.name: A thousand spaces
values.breaks: Character-by-character trimming and layouts that do not wrap; a thousand spaces is still a short value by character count.
values.expect: Rejected or trimmed - never accepted and stored in full.

packs.name: Unicode and text
packs.description: Characters that look innocent and break counting, comparison and display.

values.name: Right-to-left override
values.breaks: A direction-override character makes the text render reversed: the value shown to the user is not the value stored.
values.expect: Stripped, escaped, or displayed with the override neutralised - never rendered as-is.

values.name: Soft hyphen
values.breaks: An invisible hyphen inside a word defeats exact search and makes two identical-looking names different records.
values.expect: Stored unchanged and found by a search for Kowalski, or normalised away on save.

values.name: Combining acute accent
values.breaks: The same letter written as a base plus a combining mark compares as different from the single-character form.
values.expect: Normalised on save, or compared in a normalisation-aware way.

values.name: Stacked combining marks
values.breaks: Stacked combining marks overflow the line vertically and cover the interface around the field.
values.expect: Accepted and clipped to the box of the field, or rejected with a limit on combining marks.

values.name: Byte-order mark inside a value
values.breaks: A byte-order mark in the middle of a value survives every copy and silently breaks exact comparison.
values.expect: Stripped on save, or preserved and made visible in the interface.

values.name: Bell control character
values.breaks: A control character passed to a terminal or a log makes the output do something instead of saying something.
values.expect: Rejected or escaped before it reaches any log, terminal or report.

values.name: Full-width Latin letters
values.breaks: Full-width letters read as Latin to a human and as different characters to search, filters and uniqueness checks.
values.expect: Normalised for comparison, or accepted and consistently treated as distinct.

values.name: Mathematical bold letters
values.breaks: Mathematical letter variants defeat profanity filters and search while looking like ordinary words.
values.expect: Normalised for comparison and filtering, or rejected in fields where plain text is expected.

values.name: Upside-down letters
values.breaks: Ordinary letters from another block, used to bypass filters and to break line rendering in lists.
values.expect: Accepted as plain text without breaking the layout, and covered by the same filters as normal text.

values.name: Mixed CJK characters
values.breaks: Double-width characters break column alignment and confuse character counters that assume one character is one cell.
values.expect: Rendered and counted correctly, with column widths adapting instead of overflowing.

values.name: Arabic inside a Latin sentence
values.breaks: Right-to-left text inside a left-to-right sentence reorders on screen, so the visual order is not the stored order.
values.expect: Stored in logical order and rendered with correct isolation, so copying returns what was typed.

values.name: Emoji in a name field
values.breaks: A character outside the basic plane in a name field breaks byte-length limits and databases configured for narrow encodings.
values.expect: Stored intact or rejected with a message - never truncated mid-character.

packs.name: Length bombs
packs.description: Values sized against common limits and against the gap between a character and a byte.

values.name: Empty value
values.breaks: An empty value tests the boundary between not filled in and filled in with nothing.
values.expect: Required fields reject it with a clear message, optional fields store it as empty.

values.name: 255 characters
values.breaks: The classic column width: one character short of the limit, exactly at it, and one over it are three different code paths.
values.expect: Accepted at the limit and rejected above it, with the limit stated in the message.

values.name: 256 characters
values.breaks: One character over the classic limit, which is where silent truncation usually happens.
values.expect: Rejected with a message, never silently cut down to 255.

values.name: 254 characters
values.breaks: The value just under the limit, used to prove the limit is off by one in either direction.
values.expect: Accepted without complaint.

values.name: 1000 characters
values.breaks: Comment and description fields sized for a sentence and used for an essay.
values.expect: Accepted, or rejected with the limit stated - not accepted and truncated.

values.name: 4000 characters
values.breaks: A limit common in older database columns, and the first size at which text fields start failing quietly.
values.expect: The same rule as above, applied consistently between the interface and storage.

values.name: 65535 characters
values.breaks: The limit of the most common text column type, where crossing it usually produces a raw database error.
values.expect: A readable message instead of a database error page.

values.name: 100000 characters
values.breaks: Character counters, layout, logs and every downstream export, all at once.
values.expect: Rejected early, before the value travels through the whole system.

values.name: 128 characters, 256 bytes
values.breaks: 128 characters but 256 bytes: a field limited in bytes rejects a value the interface said was fine.
values.expect: The same unit used for the limit on both sides, and stated in the message.

values.name: 64 emoji
values.breaks: Truncation by bytes cuts the last character in half and produces a value that is no longer valid text.
values.expect: Truncation, if it happens at all, happens on character boundaries - never mid-character.

values.name: 200 characters without a space
values.breaks: 200 characters without a space: layouts that wrap on spaces push the value outside its container.
values.expect: Wrapped or clipped inside the container, never overflowing the surrounding interface.

values.name: One character
values.breaks: The shortest non-empty value, used against minimum-length rules that are rarely tested.
values.expect: Accepted or rejected according to a stated minimum, not silently accepted where a minimum exists.

packs.name: Magic values
packs.description: Words a human reads as text and a parser reads as a boolean, an absent value or a number.

values.name: The word no
values.breaks: YAML 1.1 and several config parsers read the unquoted word no as boolean false - and NO is the country code for Norway.
values.expect: Stored and returned as the two-character string no.

values.name: The word null
values.breaks: Serializers and loosely typed interfaces turn the text into an absent value; the field looks saved and comes back empty.
values.expect: Stored and returned as the four-character string, distinct from an empty field.

values.name: The word true
values.breaks: A text field holding the word true becomes a boolean somewhere in the chain and stops round-tripping.
values.expect: Returned as text, exactly as entered.

values.name: The word NaN
values.breaks: Numeric parsers accept it, and then every comparison against it is false - filters and sorting quietly drop the row.
values.expect: Rejected in a numeric field; kept verbatim in a text field.

values.name: The word Infinity
values.breaks: Accepted as a number by some layers and rejected by others, so the same value validates differently at each step.
values.expect: One consistent verdict across the interface, the service layer and storage.

values.name: The word undefined
values.breaks: Often the result of a bug elsewhere, so a real value spelled this way is indistinguishable from a defect.
values.expect: Stored and displayed as ordinary text, without special treatment.

values.name: The word yes
values.breaks: The same coercion problem as the word no, in the opposite direction, and equally invisible in review.
values.expect: Returned as the three-character string.

values.name: The word off
values.breaks: Another word coerced to a boolean by common configuration parsers.
values.expect: Returned as text.

values.name: The word None
values.breaks: The absent-value keyword in one widely used language; travels through interfaces as a null.
values.expect: Returned as the four-character string.

values.name: The word nil
values.breaks: The absent-value keyword in another; same failure, different layer.
values.expect: Returned as text.

values.name: N/A with a slash
values.breaks: Contains a separator, so it also breaks paths, CSV columns and anything splitting on a slash.
values.expect: Stored and displayed intact.

values.name: A single dash
values.breaks: A single dash is a real answer in forms and a "no value" marker in reports - the two meanings collide on export.
values.expect: Stored as a one-character value, distinguishable from an empty field.

packs.name: Extreme numbers
packs.description: Numbers at the edges of their types, in foreign notations, and where precision runs out.

values.name: Largest safe JavaScript integer plus one
values.breaks: Above this value browsers and many interfaces stop representing whole numbers exactly, so an identifier returned by the server no longer matches what the user sees.
values.expect: Handled as text where exactness matters, or rejected with a stated limit.

values.name: 32-bit integer maximum plus one
values.breaks: One past the most common integer limit - where counters, identifiers and quantities wrap to a negative number.
values.expect: Rejected with a message, or handled by a wider type consistently.

values.name: 32-bit integer maximum
values.breaks: The boundary itself: accepted here and failing one higher is the difference between a correct limit and an accident.
values.expect: Accepted where the limit allows it.

values.name: Minus one
values.breaks: Quantity, price and count fields that never expected a negative value; often accepted and only noticed at invoicing.
values.expect: Rejected wherever a negative value is meaningless, with a message that says so.

values.name: Zero
values.breaks: Distinguishing "zero" from "not filled in" is one of the most commonly confused boundaries in forms.
values.expect: Stored as zero and displayed as zero, never as an empty field.

values.name: Comma as the decimal separator
values.breaks: The decimal separator used across most of Europe; parsers expecting a dot read it as a thousands separator or reject it.
values.expect: Accepted in locales that use it, or rejected with a message naming the expected format.

values.name: Spaces between thousands
values.breaks: Copying a number out of a report brings the group separators with it; most numeric parsers refuse.
values.expect: Separators stripped before parsing, or a message explaining the expected format.

values.name: Exponential notation
values.breaks: Spreadsheet exports produce this form for large numbers, so it arrives in fields that never expected it.
values.expect: Accepted and expanded, or rejected - never read as the digit 1.

values.name: Leading zeros
values.breaks: Codes, room numbers and article numbers lose their leading zeros the moment they are treated as numbers.
values.expect: Preserved where the value is a code, not a quantity.

values.name: Typographic minus sign
values.breaks: The typographic minus sign looks identical to the ASCII one and is rejected by every numeric parser.
values.expect: Normalised before parsing, or rejected with a message that names the character.

values.name: 50 digits
values.breaks: A number wider than any numeric type; usually produces an overflow or a raw error rather than a message.
values.expect: A readable message instead of an error page.

values.name: Plus sign before a number
values.breaks: An explicitly positive number, valid in most notations and rejected by many simple validators.
values.expect: Accepted and normalised, or rejected with a stated format.

packs.name: Impossible dates
packs.description: Dates that do not exist, that are ambiguous, or that are written differently than the field assumes.

values.name: 30 February
values.breaks: A date that cannot exist; naive parsers roll it over to the second of March instead of refusing it.
values.expect: Rejected with a message - never silently moved to another day.

values.name: 29 February in a non-leap year
values.breaks: Valid in some years and not in others, so the same input is correct or incorrect depending on the year field next to it.
values.expect: Rejected for non-leap years, with the reason stated.

values.name: 31 November
values.breaks: The month-length check that most hand-written validators skip.
values.expect: Rejected, not rolled over into December.

values.name: Day and month in an ambiguous order
values.breaks: The same text means March or April depending on convention, and nothing on screen says which was assumed.
values.expect: The expected order stated next to the field, or an unambiguous format enforced.

values.name: ISO 8601 date
values.breaks: A field expecting a local format receives the international one, and vice versa; both are legitimate user input.
values.expect: Both accepted, or one enforced with a visible example.

values.name: Year 9999
values.breaks: The upper end of most date types; often accepted by the interface and rejected by storage.
values.expect: The same range enforced on both sides.

values.name: Year 0000
values.breaks: Below the range of several date types, and the year zero does not exist in the common calendar.
values.expect: Rejected with a stated range.

values.name: Five-digit year
values.breaks: Five-digit years break fixed-width parsing and column formats without producing an obvious error.
values.expect: Rejected with a stated range.

values.name: Unix epoch
values.breaks: The zero point of the most common timestamp representation; frequently indistinguishable from "no date set".
values.expect: Stored and displayed as a real date, distinct from an empty field.

values.name: Negative timestamp
values.breaks: Dates before the epoch are negative in many representations and are silently rejected or wrapped.
values.expect: Handled as an ordinary past date, or rejected with the supported range stated.

values.name: A date in words
values.breaks: Text in a date field: accepted by lenient parsers, which then produce a different date every day.
values.expect: Rejected - natural-language dates belong to a deliberate feature, not to a parser's leniency.

values.name: Slashes instead of dots
values.breaks: The same date in another separator; forms often accept one and store the other without saying so.
values.expect: Accepted in both, normalised once, and shown in one consistent form.

packs.name: Export breakers
packs.description: Values that pass validation and break only in the exported file.

values.name: Value starting with =
values.breaks: A value starting with an equals sign is treated as a formula by spreadsheet software; the exported file shows a computed result instead of the data.
values.expect: Escaped on export so the spreadsheet shows the text as entered.

values.name: Code that looks like a date
values.breaks: Spreadsheet software converts short codes that look like dates into dates, and the original value cannot be recovered from the file.
values.expect: Exported as text, with the column typed so the conversion never happens.

values.name: Comma inside a value
values.breaks: A comma inside a value splits one column into two unless the value is quoted correctly at every export step.
values.expect: Quoted on export; the file parses back into the same number of columns.

values.name: Quotation marks inside a value
values.breaks: Quotation marks inside a quoted value must be doubled; getting this wrong shifts every following column.
values.expect: Quoted and escaped so the round trip returns the original text.

values.name: Line break inside a value
values.breaks: A line break inside a value turns one row into two for every parser that splits on lines before parsing.
values.expect: Quoted so the record stays one row, or rejected at input.

values.name: Nineteen-digit identifier
values.breaks: Spreadsheets keep about fifteen significant digits, so long identifiers come back rounded and in exponential notation.
values.expect: Exported as text; the identifier survives opening and saving the file.

values.name: Code with leading zeros
values.breaks: Codes lose their leading zeros the moment a spreadsheet treats the column as numeric.
values.expect: Exported as text so the code stays as issued.

values.name: Phone number starting with +
values.breaks: A phone number written with a country prefix is read as a formula, and the cell shows an error instead of the number.
values.expect: Escaped on export, or the column typed as text.

values.name: Value starting with -
values.breaks: Same as the equals sign, in a form that also looks like an ordinary negative number.
values.expect: Escaped on export.

values.name: Value starting with @
values.breaks: A social handle or mention becomes a function call in some spreadsheet software.
values.expect: Escaped on export.

values.name: Semicolon inside a value
values.breaks: The alternative column separator used in several locales; a file correct in one locale breaks in another.
values.expect: The separator declared in the file, and values quoted regardless of which one is used.

values.name: Fraction that looks like a date
values.breaks: A fraction, a ratio or a house number, converted to a date on opening the file.
values.expect: Exported as text; opening and saving the file does not change the value.

packs.name: Polish locale
packs.description: Polish identifiers, formats and characters that global commercial products do not handle.

values.name: PESEL with a valid checksum
values.breaks: A national identifier that passes the checksum but encodes an impossible birth date - accepted by length checks, rejected by real validation.
values.expect: Accepted or rejected according to which validation the field claims to do, consistently.

values.name: PESEL with a wrong checksum
values.breaks: Differs from the valid one by a single digit; a field checking only the length cannot tell them apart.
values.expect: Rejected with a message that says the checksum failed, not that the length is wrong.

values.name: Every Polish diacritic
values.breaks: Encoding narrower than the full character set replaces these with question marks, and the name is corrupted on save.
values.expect: Stored and returned unchanged in every layer, including exports and printouts.

values.name: Double-barrelled surname
values.breaks: Double surnames break name splitting, sorting and the assumption that a surname is one word.
values.expect: Stored as one surname; sorting and search treat it as written.

values.name: Polish postal code
values.breaks: The national postal code format; a field expecting five digits without a separator rejects every real code.
values.expect: The expected format shown next to the field, and the separator handled either way.

values.name: Street with a building and flat number
values.breaks: House and flat numbers written with a slash; a field splitting on a slash produces two address lines from one.
values.expect: Stored as one line, and exported without splitting.

packs.name: File names and paths
packs.description: Names a file system rejects, alters, or reads differently than the user meant.

values.name: Reserved device name
values.breaks: A device name reserved by one operating system; a file with this name cannot be created and the failure often surfaces as a generic error.
values.expect: Rejected at input with a message naming the reserved word, not at write time.

values.name: Trailing dot
values.breaks: Trailing dots are silently removed by some file systems, so the stored name differs from the requested one.
values.expect: Rejected, or normalised visibly so the user sees the name that will be used.

values.name: Trailing space in a file name
values.breaks: A trailing space in a file name is invisible, sometimes removed and sometimes kept - two files that look identical.
values.expect: Trimmed consistently, and the resulting name shown to the user.

values.name: Characters forbidden in file names
values.breaks: Characters legal on one system and forbidden on another; a file created on one machine cannot be copied to another.
values.expect: Rejected with the forbidden characters named, before the file is created.

values.name: Double extension
values.breaks: Interfaces hiding known extensions show this as report.txt, so the user sees a document and gets a program.
values.expect: The full name shown wherever the user makes a decision about the file.

values.name: Right-to-left override in a file name
values.breaks: A direction override makes the extension read in reverse, so a program looks like a text file.
values.expect: Direction-control characters stripped or neutralised in every file name display.

values.name: A single dot
values.breaks: A single dot means "this directory"; used as a file name it either fails or does something unintended.
values.expect: Rejected at input.

values.name: Two dots
values.breaks: Two dots mean the parent directory; the shortest possible traversal test.
values.expect: Rejected at input.

values.name: Leading dot
values.breaks: A leading dot hides the file on some systems, so an uploaded file disappears from listings.
values.expect: Accepted, and listed regardless of the leading dot.

values.name: File name outside ASCII
values.breaks: Non-ASCII names break archives, transfers and any layer assuming a narrow encoding.
values.expect: Stored, listed, downloaded and archived with the name intact.

values.name: 260 characters
values.breaks: The classic path length limit; crossing it produces failures far from the place the name was entered.
values.expect: Rejected with the limit stated, at the point where the name is entered.

values.name: Space in a file name
values.breaks: Names with spaces break command construction and links that are not quoted or encoded.
values.expect: Handled everywhere the file name is used, including download links.

packs.name: Look-alike pairs
packs.description: Pairs of values that are identical on screen and different in storage.

values.name: Name with a Latin a
values.breaks: The control half of a pair - only meaningful next to its counterpart.
values.expect: Stored as typed.

values.name: Name with a Cyrillic a
values.breaks: A Cyrillic letter identical in shape to the Latin one; two accounts that look the same to every human.
values.expect: Either both accepted as distinct and shown as distinct, or the second rejected as a duplicate.

values.name: Word with a Latin o
values.breaks: The control half of a pair - only meaningful next to the Greek omicron below it.
values.expect: Stored as typed.

values.name: Word with a Greek omicron
values.breaks: The same shape from a third script; catches uniqueness checks that only handle Cyrillic.
values.expect: Same as above.

values.name: Accented word, composed
values.breaks: Control half: the accented letters written as single characters.
values.expect: Stored as typed.

values.name: Accented word, decomposed
values.breaks: The same word with combining marks; identical on screen, different in storage and in every comparison.
values.expect: Normalised on save, or compared in a normalisation-aware way.

values.name: Name with an ordinary space
values.breaks: The control half of a pair - an ordinary space, so that the non-breaking one has something to fail against.
values.expect: Stored as typed.

values.name: Name with a non-breaking space
values.breaks: A non-breaking space where an ordinary one is expected; search never matches.
values.expect: Normalised, or treated as distinct consistently.

values.name: Range with a hyphen
values.breaks: The control half of a pair, with the ASCII hyphen - it parses everywhere the dash below it does not.
values.expect: Stored as typed.

values.name: Range with an en dash
values.breaks: The typographic dash that arrives with every copy from a document; breaks parsing of ranges.
values.expect: Normalised before parsing, or accepted as an equivalent separator.

values.name: Capital i, lowercase L and one
values.breaks: Capital i, lowercase L and the digit one in one value: indistinguishable in many typefaces.
values.expect: Displayed in a typeface where the characters can be told apart, wherever the value must be read back.

values.name: Letter O and digit zero
values.breaks: The same problem for the letter O and the digit zero, in codes people retype by hand.
values.expect: Same as above, or the ambiguous characters excluded from generated codes.

packs.name: Complex emoji
packs.description: Characters beyond the basic plane and composed sequences that break counting and truncation.

values.name: Family emoji built with joiners
values.breaks: One image to the user, three characters plus two invisible joiners to the software; truncation cuts it into unrelated pictures.
values.expect: Counted and truncated as one unit, or rejected - never split between the joiners.

values.name: Emoji with a skin tone
values.breaks: A base character plus a modifier: cutting between them changes the meaning of the value.
values.expect: Kept together by any truncation.

values.name: Keycap digit one
values.breaks: A digit, a variation selector and a combining mark that together render as one key; the digit alone is a number.
values.expect: Preserved as a unit; not parsed as the number one.

values.name: Heart with a variation selector
values.breaks: The variation selector decides whether this renders as a picture or as text; stripping it silently changes the display.
values.expect: Preserved on save so the value looks the same after a round trip.

values.name: Country flag
values.breaks: A flag is two regional indicator characters; a field limited to two characters accepts it and one limited to one splits it.
values.expect: Treated as one unit for length limits.

values.name: Emoji inside a name
values.breaks: A character outside the basic plane inside a name breaks storage configured for narrow encodings, often with a raw error.
values.expect: Stored intact, or rejected with a readable message.

values.name: Ideograph beyond the basic plane
values.breaks: A rare ideograph outside the basic plane: the same storage problem without looking like an emoji.
values.expect: Handled exactly like any other character.

values.name: Fifty emoji
values.breaks: Fifty characters to the user, two hundred bytes to storage; the mismatch between limits shows up here first.
values.expect: Limits stated in the same unit on both sides.

values.name: A single emoji
values.breaks: A name or title consisting solely of a picture; sorting, initials and search all have to do something with it.
values.expect: Accepted and displayed, with sorting and initials behaving predictably.

values.name: Joiner with nothing to join
values.breaks: A joiner with nothing to join: invisible, meaningless, and enough to make two identical names different.
values.expect: Stripped on save, or preserved and revealed in the interface.

values.name: Emoji in a file name
values.breaks: Archives, transfers and older file systems handle these names inconsistently.
values.expect: Stored and downloaded with the name intact, or rejected before the file is created.

values.name: A thousand emoji
values.breaks: A thousand pictures: rendering, scrolling and every length counter at once.
values.expect: Accepted and clipped in the layout, or rejected with a stated limit.

packs.name: Encoding and mojibake
packs.description: Text that went through the wrong encoding and never came back.

values.name: Text encoded twice
values.breaks: Text encoded twice: it displays as nonsense and, once saved in this state, the original cannot be recovered.
values.expect: Never produced - and if received, stored verbatim rather than "fixed" by guessing.

values.name: Byte-order mark before a name
values.breaks: A byte-order mark at the start of a value makes exact comparison fail and sorts the record before everything else.
values.expect: Stripped on input, consistently in every layer that reads files.

values.name: Replacement character in a name
values.breaks: The character that appears where decoding already failed; its presence means data was lost earlier.
values.expect: Detected and reported rather than stored as if it were ordinary text.

values.name: Question marks for lost letters
values.breaks: What narrow encodings produce instead of characters they cannot represent - indistinguishable from a user typing question marks.
values.expect: Never produced: the full character set supported end to end.

values.name: Accented letter at the end
values.breaks: A common accented word that survives or breaks depending on the encoding of each layer it passes through.
values.expect: Identical before and after a save-and-reload round trip.

values.name: Letters from regional encodings
values.breaks: Letters present in regional encodings and absent from others; the first thing to break in an export.
values.expect: Preserved in exports, printouts and file names.

values.name: One Cyrillic letter in a Latin name
values.breaks: One Cyrillic letter inside a Latin word - the value looks correct and never matches a search.
values.expect: Either normalised or flagged; not silently accepted as if identical.

values.name: Emoji, ideograph and Arabic together
values.breaks: Emoji, an ideograph and an Arabic letter in one value: three different storage assumptions at once.
values.expect: Stored and returned unchanged.

values.name: Ideographic space in a name
values.breaks: An ideographic space: a real space character that most trimming routines do not know about.
values.expect: Trimmed like any other whitespace, or preserved consistently.

values.name: Letter with five combining accents
values.breaks: Many combining marks on one letter: normalisation and length limits disagree about how many characters this is.
values.expect: Counted consistently, and rendered without covering neighbouring interface.

values.name: Every risky class in one value
values.breaks: A single value combining every risky class, for a quick save-and-reload check.
values.expect: Returned byte-for-byte identical after a full round trip.

packs.name: Pasted from a document
packs.description: Characters that arrive with text copied out of a word processor or a web page.

values.name: Typographic apostrophe
values.breaks: The typographic apostrophe arrives with every paste and is a different character from the one on the keyboard; search never matches.
values.expect: Normalised on save, or both forms treated as equivalent by search.

values.name: Curly quotation marks
values.breaks: Curly quotation marks break parsers, command construction and any comparison against the straight form.
values.expect: Accepted and stored; normalised before anything parses the value.

values.name: Em dash between words
values.breaks: The long dash pasted from a document where a hyphen was expected; range parsing and code matching stop working.
values.expect: Normalised before parsing, or accepted as an equivalent separator.

values.name: Range with an en dash
values.breaks: A range that looks correct and parses as a single unknown token.
values.expect: Same as above.

values.name: Non-breaking space from a document
values.breaks: Text editors insert non-breaking spaces automatically; the value looks normal and never matches an exact search.
values.expect: Normalised to an ordinary space, or found by search regardless.

values.name: Soft hyphen inside a word
values.breaks: Optional hyphens survive copying and split a word invisibly in storage.
values.expect: Stripped on save, or preserved and revealed in the interface.

values.name: Ellipsis character
values.breaks: One character that looks like three dots; length limits and comparisons disagree with what the user sees.
values.expect: Counted as one character, or normalised to three dots consistently.

values.name: Bullet from a list
values.breaks: A bullet pasted from a list turns a value into something that renders as a list item elsewhere.
values.expect: Stored as text, without being interpreted as formatting.

values.name: Non-breaking hyphen in a code
values.breaks: A non-breaking hyphen inside a code; visually identical to the ordinary one, different everywhere else.
values.expect: Normalised before validation of the code.

values.name: Zero-width space from a web page
values.breaks: Web pages insert zero-width characters for layout; they arrive with the copied text and stay forever.
values.expect: Stripped on save, or revealed in the interface.

values.name: Everything a document pastes
values.breaks: Everything at once, as it actually arrives from a document.
values.expect: Round-trips unchanged, and is found by a search typed on a keyboard.

values.name: Trailing non-breaking space
values.breaks: A non-breaking space at the end: invisible, not removed by ordinary trimming, and enough to break a comparison.
values.expect: Trimmed together with ordinary whitespace.

packs.name: E-mail addresses and URLs
packs.description: Addresses that are formally valid but extreme, and ones that only look valid.

values.name: Plus tag in the local part
values.breaks: A perfectly valid address rejected by a surprising number of forms, which breaks the tagging people rely on.
values.expect: Accepted; the plus sign is a legal character in the local part.

values.name: Uppercase local part
values.breaks: The local part is case-sensitive in principle and treated as case-insensitive in practice; uniqueness checks disagree between layers.
values.expect: One consistent rule, applied at sign-up and at sign-in alike.

values.name: Internationalised domain
values.breaks: Internationalised domains must be converted before use; a form that skips this rejects legitimate addresses.
values.expect: Accepted and converted, or rejected with a message that says why.

values.name: Two at signs
values.breaks: The shortest invalid address that many simple validators accept.
values.expect: Rejected.

values.name: Address without an at sign
values.breaks: A domain typed into an e-mail field; accepted by validators that only check for a dot.
values.expect: Rejected.

values.name: Trailing dot after the domain
values.breaks: A trailing dot is technically valid in a domain name and rejected by nearly every form.
values.expect: Accepted and normalised, or rejected consistently.

values.name: Local part of 64 characters
values.breaks: The boundary of the local part length; one character more must be rejected.
values.expect: The limit enforced with a message, not by truncation.

values.name: Quoted local part with a space
values.breaks: A quoted local part containing a space is legal and almost never handled.
values.expect: Accepted, or rejected with a message stating the supported subset.

values.name: Link without a scheme
values.breaks: A link typed the way people type links; storing it without a scheme produces a broken link everywhere it is used.
values.expect: Normalised with a scheme, or rejected with an example of the expected form.

values.name: Link with credentials
values.breaks: A URL carrying credentials; displaying it anywhere reveals them, and storing it keeps them.
values.expect: Rejected, or stored with the credentials stripped and the user told.

values.name: Link of 2000 characters
values.breaks: Long links break storage limits, logs and every column that displays them.
values.expect: Accepted up to a stated limit, and truncated for display only.

values.name: Link with a non-ASCII path
values.breaks: Non-ASCII paths must be encoded; a layer that skips it produces links that work in one place and not another.
values.expect: Encoded once and consistently; the link works after a round trip.

packs.name: Names and identity
packs.description: Names that break assumptions about what a "normal" name looks like.

values.name: Surname Null
values.breaks: A real surname that every layer treating text loosely turns into an absent value; the record loses its name on save.
values.expect: Stored and displayed as a four-letter surname, distinct from an empty field.

values.name: Single name only
values.breaks: People with one name exist; a form requiring both parts cannot represent them at all.
values.expect: Accepted with one name filled in, without inventing a placeholder for the other.

values.name: Surname with an apostrophe
values.breaks: The apostrophe breaks query construction, name splitting and sorting; the most common real surname that breaks forms.
values.expect: Stored, displayed, searched and sorted exactly as written.

values.name: Two surnames without a hyphen
values.breaks: Two surnames without a hyphen; splitting on the space produces a wrong first name.
values.expect: Kept as one surname; splitting, if any, is a deliberate feature rather than a guess.

values.name: Surname with lowercase particles
values.breaks: Lowercase particles break capitalisation, sorting and any rule assuming a surname starts with a capital letter.
values.expect: Stored as written; sorting rules stated rather than assumed.

values.name: One-letter name
values.breaks: A one-letter name is legal in several countries and rejected by nearly every minimum-length rule.
values.expect: Accepted, or the minimum stated with a reason.

values.name: Surname in capitals
values.breaks: Names written in capitals, common on documents; auto-capitalisation turns them into something else.
values.expect: Stored as entered; automatic capitalisation, if any, is visible and reversible.

values.name: Digit in a name
values.breaks: Digits in a name break validators that allow letters only, and those validators reject legitimate users.
values.expect: Accepted, or a stated rule explaining the restriction.

values.name: Name of 120 characters
values.breaks: Long names hit column limits and layouts sized for a typical name.
values.expect: Accepted up to a stated limit and displayed without breaking the layout.

values.name: Title typed into the name
values.breaks: Titles typed into a name field break salutations and duplicate detection.
values.expect: Stored as written; the salutation composed without assuming the field contains only a name.

values.name: Hyphenated given name
values.breaks: A hyphenated given name splits into two in systems assuming one word per field.
values.expect: Kept as one given name.

values.name: Surname True
values.breaks: The same failure as Null in a different form, and one that also breaks configuration files.
values.expect: Stored and displayed as written.

packs.name: Time and time zones
packs.description: Hours that do not exist, happen twice, or are written without a zone.

values.name: Hour skipped by the spring clock change
values.breaks: On the day clocks go forward in central Europe this hour does not exist locally; parsers either shift it silently or fail with a raw error.
values.expect: Rejected with an explanation, or shifted with the shift shown to the user.

values.name: Hour repeated by the autumn clock change
values.breaks: On the day clocks go back in central Europe this hour happens twice; without a zone the value cannot be resolved to a moment.
values.expect: The zone requested, or one interpretation chosen and stated.

values.name: Timestamp without a zone
values.breaks: A timestamp without a zone is meaningless the moment it crosses a machine boundary, and it always does.
values.expect: Rejected, or interpreted with the assumed zone stated next to the value.

values.name: Timestamp with an offset
values.breaks: The correct form; a field rejecting it accepts only the ambiguous one.
values.expect: Accepted and preserved, including the offset.

values.name: Timestamp in UTC
values.breaks: The same moment written in the universal form; storing it as local time loses two hours somewhere.
values.expect: Accepted and converted for display, not stored as if it were local.

values.name: Date and time as people type them
values.breaks: The format people actually type; a field accepting only the international one rejects every human.
values.expect: Accepted with the expected format shown, or both accepted.

values.name: Midnight written as 24:00
values.breaks: Midnight at the end of the day: valid in the international notation and rejected by most parsers.
values.expect: Accepted and normalised to the next day's zero hour, or rejected with a message.

values.name: Leap second
values.breaks: The sixty-first second exists in the standard and in no common date type.
values.expect: Rejected with a message, or clamped visibly - not accepted and silently shifted.

values.name: Start of the Unix epoch
values.breaks: The zero point of the most common timestamp; indistinguishable from "no time set" in many interfaces.
values.expect: Displayed as a real moment, distinct from an empty field.

values.name: Last second of 2099
values.breaks: Far dates break retention rules, schedulers and columns with a narrower range than the interface.
values.expect: Accepted up to a stated range, enforced on both sides.

values.name: Timestamp eleven hours behind UTC
values.breaks: An offset far from the server's own; sorting by local time produces a different order than sorting by moment.
values.expect: Sorted and compared by moment, not by the text of the timestamp.

values.name: Time without a date
values.breaks: A time without a date; storing it against today's date changes its meaning tomorrow.
values.expect: Stored as a time of day, or the date requested explicitly.

packs.name: Money and separators
packs.description: Amounts written the way people and spreadsheets write them, and where precision ends.

values.name: Rounding trap 2,675
values.breaks: Rounded to two places this value goes down where a human expects it to go up, because the binary representation is slightly below the decimal one.
values.expect: Rounded by a rule stated in the specification, applied identically in the interface and in storage.

values.name: Rounding trap 1,005
values.breaks: The same failure at a different magnitude; one of the two catches almost every naive rounding implementation.
values.expect: Same as above.

values.name: Comma as the decimal separator
values.breaks: The decimal separator used locally; a parser expecting a dot reads it as a thousands separator and multiplies the amount by a hundred.
values.expect: Accepted in locales that use it, with the expected format shown.

values.name: Non-breaking spaces between thousands
values.breaks: Amounts copied from a report carry non-breaking spaces as group separators, which no numeric parser accepts.
values.expect: Separators stripped before parsing, including the invisible ones.

values.name: Spaces between thousands
values.breaks: The same with ordinary spaces - the form produced by most local formatting.
values.expect: Accepted and normalised.

values.name: Negative amount in brackets
values.breaks: Accounting notation for negative amounts; read as text it becomes a positive number in brackets.
values.expect: Interpreted as negative, or rejected with the expected form shown.

values.name: Three decimal places
values.breaks: More decimal places than the currency has; silently rounding here changes an invoice total.
values.expect: Rejected, or rounded with the rounding shown before saving.

values.name: Negative zero
values.breaks: A negative zero displays as a negative amount and compares equal to zero; reports show a minus sign on nothing.
values.expect: Normalised to zero on save.

values.name: Zero amount
values.breaks: Zero is a legitimate amount and is frequently confused with an empty field.
values.expect: Stored and displayed as zero, distinct from empty.

values.name: Amount with the currency symbol
values.breaks: The amount as it appears in a document, with the currency symbol; a numeric field rejects it whole.
values.expect: The symbol stripped on input, or the expected form shown.

values.name: Apostrophe between thousands
values.breaks: The group separator used in some locales; unfamiliar and perfectly legitimate.
values.expect: Accepted where that locale is supported, or rejected with the expected form.

values.name: Amount wider than the money type
values.breaks: An amount wider than the type used for money; overflow here produces a negative total.
values.expect: Rejected with a stated limit, before it reaches any total.

packs.name: Pseudolocalisation
packs.description: The standard internationalisation-testing technique, reduced to values you can paste into a field.

values.name: Pseudolocalised text in brackets
values.breaks: The brackets reveal truncation instantly: if either is missing on screen, the text was cut.
values.expect: Both brackets visible wherever the value is displayed.

values.name: Accented pseudolocalised word
values.breaks: Still readable as English, so a tester spots it in a screen where a string was never translated.
values.expect: Displayed with every accent intact, in every layer.

values.name: Pseudolocalised text, 30 per cent longer
values.breaks: Thirty per cent longer, the typical growth when English is translated into German.
values.expect: The layout holds without clipping or overlapping.

values.name: Pseudolocalised text, twice as long
values.breaks: Twice the length, for labels and buttons sized to the English word.
values.expect: Wrapped or resized rather than clipped.

values.name: Very short pseudolocalised text
values.breaks: The opposite case: a very short translation leaves a layout built around a long one looking broken.
values.expect: The layout holds when the value is short.

values.name: Pseudolocalised text with direction marks
values.breaks: Pseudolocalisation with direction marks, for checking mirrored layouts without knowing a right-to-left language.
values.expect: The interface mirrors correctly and the brackets stay in the right places.

values.name: Number inside pseudolocalised text
values.breaks: Numbers inside a pseudolocalised string reveal formatting that was hard-coded next to the text.
values.expect: Numbers formatted by locale, not concatenated.

values.name: Placeholder inside pseudolocalised text
values.breaks: A placeholder that must survive translation; losing it produces a message with a hole in it.
values.expect: The placeholder preserved and filled.

values.name: Markup inside pseudolocalised text
values.breaks: Markup inside a translated string is either escaped or rendered, and both are wrong in different places.
values.expect: Handled the same way as any other user-provided markup in that field.

values.name: Three scripts in one string
values.breaks: Three scripts in one string: font fallback, line breaking and direction all at once.
values.expect: Every script rendered, with no missing-glyph boxes.
